solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 'Giddy-up' and irritate the creature

definitions.meaning: a call to a horse to get going, so an order to hurry
to make an animal tetchy and inclined to bite

explanation.surface: A rider urging a horse on and annoying the animal at the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase two ways: as an order to be quick, and literally as 'make it (the creature) snappy', meaning bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a brusque instruction to hurry, just as a rider's shout urges a horse to speed up.

clue.text: Attaching to low loop

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
a ring is a loop

explanation.surface: Fixing something to a small hoop near the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' looks like an adjective but is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring is tying up a boat, fastening it to a buoy or quay.

clue.text: Have successful reunion after getting plastered

definitions.text: Have successful reunion after getting plastered

parts.words: Have successful reunion after getting plastered
parts.note: describes broken bones mending after being set in a plaster cast

explanation.surface: Old friends getting drunk and having a great get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' suggests drunk, but it is a plaster cast on a fracture.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken bones are said to mend together, joining up again as they heal.

clue.text: Under cover, I burnt having caught sun terribly

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the scrambled star inside them

parts.note: sunburnt skin is red

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sheltering after getting badly sunburnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' scrambles the star and 'having caught' holds it inside I plus the burnt colour; 'Under cover' means protected by a policy, not hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under cover means having a policy that protects against loss or damage.

clue.text: To mollify, put little arm round

indicators.note: the weapon is put round the small word, which sits inside

parts.note: the Sten was a British submachine gun, an arm
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Calming someone by putting a small arm around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb, but it is the Sten gun, which goes round WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften or placate someone is to make them more agreeable, as sugar does a drink.

clue.text: Vera is with it, when it comes to cosmetics

definitions.text: Vera is with it, when it comes to cosmetics

parts.words: Vera is with it, when it comes to cosmetics
parts.note: the plant name that pairs with vera to name a skincare ingredient

explanation.surface: A woman named Vera is trendy where make-up is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vera' looks like a woman's name; in cosmetics it is the second word of a plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Its sap, from the species named vera, is a soothing ingredient in many skin creams.

clue.text: Off the record, I laid on tax cuts before

indicators.note: the letters cut into the word for before, splitting it

parts.note: pre means before, as a prefix

indicators.note: in a down entry the letter is laid on top of the tax

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: An anonymous source admitting they imposed tax cuts earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid on' puts I above VAT, and 'cuts' sends IVAT into PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said privately is confidential, not for the public record.

clue.text: Chef rants: 'Drum out hot stuff!'

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook ranting at someone to drive off a lustful type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CHEF RANTS DRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dijon-style condiment is a spicy, pungent seasoning, so literally hot.

clue.text: Either segregated the healthy or didn't interfere

definitions.meaning: put the fit people to one side, by themselves

explanation.surface: A quarantine choice: isolate the healthy, or just stay out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, it is leaving the well people alone; as an idiom, it is not meddling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means refraining from touching or meddling with something best left as it is.

clue.text: Skier's shown off, circling round and round novices

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the two circles that follow
something shown off is put on display in a new light, so these letters are set out in a fresh order

parts.note: the skier, with the 's standing for 'is', a link
a round thing is a ring, the letter O
a second ring, another letter O

explanation.surface: A showy skier performing loops around beginners on the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown off' rearranges SKIER, and 'circling' puts that around OO, the two rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rookies are beginners or recruits, people new to an activity.

clue.text: Upsetting book — yours truly has exciting feelings

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, so the book's letters are turned the other way

parts.note: a tome is a large book
yours truly is the speaker, I, and 'I have' contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A distressing novel stirs up its writer's own emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' turns TOME into EMOT; 'yours truly has' gives I'VE, the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotive arouses strong emotion, stirring up a reader's passions.

clue.text: Catch somebody slow but not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the slow creature is dropped

parts.note: a snail is a byword for a slow person

explanation.surface: A plea to catch a dawdler, but not right away.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a culprit is to catch or pin them down, a common informal sense.

clue.text: Wild creature that is captured

indicators.note: the creature is held inside the abbreviation, as a prisoner is

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
a rat is a common creature

explanation.surface: A wild animal that has been trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild here means furious, so an angry person is said to be wild with rage.

clue.text: Vehicle reversing, some going forwards

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A car backing up while others drive forwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap reversed, read going forwards, is a word meaning some.
explanation.definitionFit: A part is a portion or some of a whole, as in 'part of the cake'.

clue.text: Not initially bright: not fine

indicators.note: the opening letter of the clever word is dropped

parts.note: brainy means bright, clever

explanation.surface: A weather report: dull at first, then not fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bright' looks like weather but means clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine weather is dry and sunny, so wet weather with showers is the reverse.

clue.text: Master running, now back again

indicators.note: running suggests movement out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the word for again is read backwards

parts.note: re- means again, as a prefix

explanation.surface: A dog's master heading back on another run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges NOW to OWN; 'back' reverses RE to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is someone who owns something, such as a dog or a slave.

clue.text: Tough gag to crack, admitted author

indicators.note: the tough word lets the cracked joke in among its letters

parts.note: hard means tough, as a hard nut is

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it up, so the joke's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A writer confessing a joke was hard to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crack' scrambles the joke and 'admitted' lets it in just after the first letter of the tough word. H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Rider Haggard was a Victorian novelist, best known for adventure stories such as She.

clue.text: Not getting any prizes but two presents

definitions.meaning: unplaced, out of the running in a race or contest
two words for present, one of time (at this moment) and one of place (in this spot), run together

explanation.surface: Someone who wins nothing but still receives a couple of gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts but means two senses of 'present': NOW for time and HERE for place.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that finishes out of the places is said to come in unplaced, with no prize at all.

clue.text: Ensure door can't swing open when you drive round the bend

definitions.meaning: take a door off its hinges, read literally
to drive someone mad, an idiom

explanation.surface: Fixing a door shut, or driving a car round a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive round the bend' looks like motoring, but it is the idiom for driving someone crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbalance someone's mind is to make them deranged, the figurative sense of the hinge removal.

clue.text: Team being one down, following are told to cheer

indicators.note: the team's number comes after, following the other piece

parts.note: when you are told something, you hear it
a football or cricket team is eleven, and one down leaves ten

explanation.surface: A team a player short, told to raise their spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Team being one down' gives TEN, eleven minus one.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage them and lift their spirits.

clue.text: Qualify, needing points to top championship

indicators.note: in a down entry the compass points sit on top of the championship

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
a title is a championship

explanation.surface: Qualifying by scoring enough points to win the championship.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give someone a right or make them eligible for something.

clue.text: Among various places, one in particular

indicators.note: the single letter goes in among the shuffled letters
various suggests different forms, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Choosing one particular spot from a range of locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges PLACES, and 'Among' slips I, for one, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Special and particular are synonyms, both meaning specific or distinct from the rest.

clue.text: Don't save it up for investment. You've earned it

indicators.note: invested means put in, so the reversed word is placed inside

parts.note: to spend is the opposite of saving

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Financial advice: don't hoard your pay, invest it, you earned it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns 'it' upside down in this down entry, and 'for investment' means it is put into the word for not saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed salary or allowance paid for work, such as a clergyman's.

clue.text: Not written charges?

definitions.meaning: split as two words, spoken ..., orally

explanation.walkthrough: Split it 2,5 for the spoken sense; whole, it is a bill for goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of charges is a document listing the amounts owed for goods or services.

clue.text: Until now, it's always been regarded as ugly

definitions.text: it's always been regarded as ugly

parts.note: to can mean until, as in 'from nine to five'
AD, anno domini, labels the era we are living in now

explanation.surface: Something has always been thought unattractive, up to the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: The warty amphibian is the traditional emblem of ugliness in folklore and fairy tales.

clue.text: Mark is terribly antisocial when half cut

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled
only the first half of the word is kept, the rest cut off

explanation.surface: A mark of shame for antisocial behaviour while drunk ('half cut' is British slang for tipsy).
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' keeps ANTIS, the first five letters of ANTISOCIAL, and 'terribly' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a mark or blemish, whether on cloth or on a reputation.

clue.text: To be in recession is diabolical

indicators.note: receding means moving back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Living through an economic downturn is terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolical means devilish, and wickedness of that kind is the core sense here.

clue.text: Dog makes annoyance audible

indicators.note: audible means as heard, so the word for annoyance is spoken

parts.note: pique is irritation or resentment

explanation.surface: A dog letting everyone hear its irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese is a small toy dog breed with a flat face, shortened to Peke.

clue.text: What door supplier verbally promises for tomorrow, not today?

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the promised treat is said out loud

parts.note: the jam of the Lewis Carroll line: jam tomorrow and jam yesterday, but never jam today

explanation.surface: A door supplier promising delivery tomorrow, never today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam tomorrow' is a British phrase for promises of good things that never arrive, from Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is a side post of a doorframe, which holds up and supports the door.

clue.text: Turn back to front

parts.note: read literally, turn your back to the front line in battle, that is withdraw

explanation.surface: An instruction to put something on the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a garment back to front; read as soldiers turning their backs on the front, it describes withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: An army that withdraws from the battle line turns its back on the enemy.

clue.text: What author won't feel at having first story returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the combined letters run backwards

parts.note: No. 1, written NO and the Roman numeral I, means first
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A writer's disappointment when their first story comes back rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses NOITALE. The definition works because a rejected author feels the opposite of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer whose manuscript is sent back unpublished will feel dejection, the opposite of great joy.

clue.text: Fickle, as hangers-on are not

definitions.meaning: changeable, not to be relied on
hangers-on are dependants, so they are depend-able, able to depend; the opposite has the negative prefix

explanation.surface: Hangers-on described as unreliable, the opposite of what one might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: dependants depend, so they are dependable in a punning sense; not so is un-dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fickle changes loyalties easily and so cannot be relied on.
